purpose: Ketoprofen is used to relieve pain, reduce swelling, and lower fever. It is commonly used for arthritis, menstrual cramps, and general pain relief. Doctors may also prescribe it after injuries or minor surgeries to help manage discomfort.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling, and fever. Ketoprofen works by blocking the enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2) that produce these chemicals. By reducing prostaglandins, the medication helps you feel less pain and reduces inflammation in your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include upset stomach, nausea, heartburn, or indigestion. Some people may also experience headaches, dizziness, or diarrhea. Taking it with food or milk can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: Ketoprofen can increase the risk of stomach ulcers or bleeding, especially if you take it for a long time or in high doses. It may also raise the risk of heart attack or stroke, so people with heart disease should use it with caution. Avoid taking it if you are pregnant, especially in the last trimester, and always tell your doctor about all other medications you take since it can interact with blood thinners and other NSAIDs.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 25 to 75 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day, or an extended-release capsule of 100 to 200 mg taken once daily. Always take the lowest effective dose for the shortest time needed. Never exceed 300 mg per day unless specifically directed by your doctor.
